decisions.title: Ready for your close-up
decisions.situation: Jordan points a phone camera at you. You can see yourself on the screen. Your nose deserves further investigation.

choices.label: Move right up to the lens
Wave at the small person on screen
Turn around at the crucial moment

result.title: Mostly nostril
result.body: Jordan keeps the picture. It is a bold choice of composition.

journal.text: I gave Jordan a very close view of my nose.

decisions.title: A principled disagreement
decisions.situation: Jordan says shoes are necessary for going outside. You were not consulted during the drafting of this policy.

choices.label: Let Jordan help
Insist on doing it yourself
Present a floor-based protest

result.title: Terms accepted
result.body: Both shoes make it onto the correct feet. A surprisingly productive morning.

journal.text: I let Jordan help with my shoes.

decisions.title: Launch delayed
decisions.situation: You turn a cardboard box into a rocket. Jordan says dinner is ready. Mission Control has terrible timing.

choices.label: Invite Jordan aboard
Finish one last countdown
Refuse to return to Earth

result.title: Crew shortage solved
result.body: Jordan puts one foot in the box. The rocket is now full.

journal.text: My cardboard rocket carried me and one of Jordan’s feet.

decisions.title: Hotel living room
decisions.situation: You ask Jordan whether you can camp in the living room. Your packing list contains six cushions and no clothes.

choices.label: Help make a proper sleeping spot
Ask Jordan to camp too
Decide your bed is better

result.title: Room with a sofa
result.body: Jordan helps you set up, then checks on you before bed.

journal.text: I camped in the living room with Jordan’s help.

decisions.title: The staffroom boss fight
decisions.situation: You copied your school map from a video game. Taylor wants to know why the staffroom is labelled “FINAL BOSS” and the toilets contain treasure.

choices.label: Replace the monsters with actual rooms
Ask whether the staffroom really is off limits
Insist the treasure is in the toilets

result.title: A less dangerous school
result.body: You redraw the map. The dragon becomes the library. Taylor marks the corrected version and circles the one staircase you accidentally kept.

journal.text: I replaced a video-game map with a real map of my school.

decisions.title: Secrets bingo
decisions.situation: For indoor break, Avery makes bingo cards out of everyone’s embarrassing habits. Your square says “cries at cartoons”. They beg you not to add their baby nickname.

choices.label: Make everyone write their own square
Give a fake sob every time your square comes up
Announce their baby nickname to the room

result.title: Voluntary humiliation
result.body: You admit that cartoon dogs get to you. Someone else confesses to eating a paper cupcake case. Avery quietly removes half the original cards.

journal.text: I turned Avery’s secrets bingo into a game of voluntary confessions.

decisions.title: An impressive illegal start
decisions.situation: You start a practice race before Taylor blows the whistle. You are winning by an enormous amount.

choices.label: Stop and restart fairly
Finish and demand a medal
Laugh and wait for the next race

result.title: Same starting line
result.body: You run again with everyone else. It is harder when they are moving too.

journal.text: I restarted a practice race after jumping the whistle.

decisions.title: Indoor architecture
decisions.situation: Rain cancels your afternoon plans. Two chairs and a blanket suggest a career in questionable structural engineering.

choices.label: Build an elaborate fort
Read by the window
Declare the whole day ruined

result.title: Approved for immediate occupancy
result.body: It collapses twice. The third version has a reading corner.

journal.text: I built a blanket fort that almost met building regulations.

decisions.title: A very short biography
decisions.situation: Avery passes you a homemade book called “People Who Smell Weird”. Your name is on page one. Every other page is blank.

choices.label: Give it a terrible review
Ask why they made it about you
Write their name on every remaining page

result.title: Needs more characters
result.body: You write “repetitive, poorly researched” on the cover. Avery laughs, then admits they could not think of a second chapter.

journal.text: I reviewed Avery’s insulting homemade book as a disappointed critic.

decisions.title: Nobody told the spy
decisions.situation: You catch Avery explaining your secret code to everyone. They claim it is fine because they have invented a second, more secret code. You have not been told it.

choices.label: Demand to inspect the new codebook
Invent a silent signal for “you are fired”
Tell everyone the first code means nothing

result.title: One unhelpful entry
result.body: The new codebook contains one word: “banana”. Avery says its meaning is classified. You add a second word meaning “tell your partner things”.

journal.text: I inspected Avery’s replacement secret code and found one word.

decisions.title: The microphone is still on
decisions.situation: After a class announcement, Avery whispers that the school jingle sounds like a microwave. The microphone is still on.

choices.label: Switch it off and warn them
Help make a short apology
Add microwave sound effects

result.title: Broadcast ends
result.body: Most people heard the first comment. You prevent a second one.

journal.text: I switched off a live microphone before Avery said anything worse.

decisions.title: Against compulsory naps
decisions.situation: Taylor assigns you to argue against replacing homework with compulsory naps. Avery gets the other side and immediately pretends to fall asleep.

choices.label: Build the strongest anti-nap case
Rehearse against Avery
Refuse to betray the nap movement

result.title: Evidence against your interests
result.body: You produce a solid argument about lost learning time. A yawn halfway through the speech complicates your position, but the work earns its marks.

journal.text: I prepared a class debate against replacing homework with naps.

decisions.title: Do teenagers smell fear?
decisions.situation: Jordan asks you to fix their phone. An open draft says, “Do teenagers smell fear? Mine only appears when the fridge opens.” They suddenly offer to fix it themselves.

choices.label: Offer an answer from a qualified teenager
Fix it without mentioning the draft
Send their contacts a mocking reading of it

result.title: Mostly, we smell cheese
result.body: Jordan laughs and admits they were having a moan. You fix the phone, then both turn towards the sound of the fridge opening.

journal.text: I caught Jordan complaining about me and answered their question about teenagers.

decisions.title: One star. Still hungry.
decisions.situation: Avery drafts a fake restaurant review of the school canteen. It includes the phrase “structural pasta”.

choices.label: Turn it into useful feedback
Keep the joke between you
Read it aloud in class

result.title: Less funny, more useful
result.body: You keep the specific complaints and remove the insults. Taylor helps pass it on.

journal.text: I helped Avery turn a canteen rant into useful feedback.

decisions.title: Your debut single is chemistry
decisions.situation: Avery secretly records you singing chemistry definitions and adds a dance beat. The file is called “Desperate for Zinc”. They want to send it to the class.

choices.label: Make them delete the recording
Demand credit as the anonymous vocalist
Record a completely unnecessary key change

result.title: An extremely limited release
result.body: Avery deletes it while you watch. They call you difficult. You call them a record label with no permission forms.

journal.text: I made Avery delete a secret recording of my chemistry revision song.

decisions.title: A beautiful baby cabbage
decisions.situation: A fair organiser needs one more judge for a vegetable baby contest. Someone pushes a cabbage in a bonnet towards you. Its grower is waiting for a score and looks ready to take this personally.

choices.label: Judge the cabbage’s personality
Disclose that you eat cabbage
Give it a terrible score for poor eye contact

result.title: A quiet, grounded child
result.body: You praise its composure and excellent leaves. The grower wipes away a tear. A rival arrives with a swaddled turnip and demands equal time.

journal.text: I praised a bonnet-wearing cabbage at a vegetable baby contest.

decisions.title: The compliment has the wrong address
decisions.situation: Someone praises an anonymous poem you were standing beside at a free exhibition. You did not write it. They are waiting for you to explain its “raw emotional honesty”.

choices.label: Thank them, then admit it is not yours
Point out the actual poet’s name
Accept the praise and invent your inspiration

result.title: A narrow escape from poetry
result.body: They laugh at the mix-up. You both admit you were not entirely sure what the last line meant.

journal.text: I corrected a stranger who thought I had written a poem.

decisions.title: Inner peace is on hold
decisions.situation: At a free relaxation class, the instructor tells you to release your anger. Their phone rings. They spend the next minute shouting at a printer repair company.

choices.label: Close your eyes and let them finish
Find peace on a walk outside
Offer to fix the printer problem

result.title: A guided loss of temper
result.body: You breathe slowly through an argument about toner. By the time they hang up, you are considerably calmer than the professional.

journal.text: I relaxed through my relaxation instructor’s furious printer call.

decisions.title: You must make the most of it
decisions.situation: You feel better rested than usual and immediately begin planning enough tasks to use every available bit of energy.

choices.label: Choose a few priorities and leave room
Enjoy feeling well without a quota
Fill every bit of the day

result.title: A useful day with an ending
result.body: You use some energy without treating all of it as a resource that must be exhausted.

journal.text: I paced a good day instead of filling every available moment.

decisions.title: A striking resemblance
decisions.situation: A caricaturist at a street fair in Los Angeles offers you a free sample portrait. A small crowd gathers. The artist turns the drawing around. It is you as an enormous angry thumb.

choices.label: Ask whether they could add a jawline
Ask for a pencil and draw the artist
Cover the portrait and leave

result.title: The formal thumb
result.body: The artist adds a bow tie. You point out that this is not a jawline. A spectator says the resemblance is uncanny. You leave holding a thumb in evening wear.

journal.text: I asked a caricaturist to correct my portrait and received a thumb in a bow tie.

decisions.title: The quiet place has noises
decisions.situation: You sit somewhere quiet and immediately notice a clock, a distant door and somebody clearing their throat. Apparently quiet did not mean perfectly silent.

choices.label: Let the ordinary sounds be there
Choose one steady sound to notice
Identify every interruption

result.title: Quiet enough is available
result.body: You stop checking each sound for a reason to be irritated. The place becomes restful without becoming silent.

journal.text: I accepted ordinary background sounds in a quiet moment.

decisions.title: Your murderous past
decisions.situation: A walking-tour guide points straight at you and tells the group you are the ghost of a notorious murderer. You are outside a shop in Los Angeles, holding a sandwich.

choices.label: Explain that you are alive and eating lunch
Ask what crimes you supposedly committed
Follow the tour without breaking eye contact

result.title: New evidence
result.body: The guide calls your sandwich an unsettling detail. You take a large bite. A tourist asks whether ghosts can eat cheese. The guide moves the group along.

journal.text: I corrected a walking tour that mistook me for a murderer’s ghost in Los Angeles.

decisions.title: Water with a personal brand
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, a presenter claims their water has been “emotionally filtered”. The jug beside it is labelled TAP. You are just thirsty.

choices.label: Drink the tap water
Ask which emotions the filter removes
Debate the emotional lives of liquids

result.title: No emotional processing required
result.body: It tastes like water. The presenter watches you finish a glass with the expression of someone witnessing sabotage.

journal.text: I chose tap water at a premium-water demonstration.

decisions.title: Doing nothing, attendance required
decisions.situation: You put “Do absolutely nothing” in your calendar. The app sends invitations to a discussion group. Six people accept and one asks about the dress code.

choices.label: Cancel it and protect your hour
Host exactly five minutes of nothing
Send an agenda for competitive relaxing

result.title: A successful cancellation
result.body: You explain that it was private. Someone replies that they were really looking forward to nothing. You enjoy it without them.

journal.text: I cancelled accidental invitations to my free hour.

decisions.title: Your shoulders have a complaint
decisions.situation: After sitting in the same position for a while, you notice that your shoulders appear to have crept up towards your ears.

choices.label: Take a gentle movement break
Change your position and relax your shoulders
Stay exactly as you are

result.title: A different position helps
result.body: You loosen up at a comfortable pace and return to what you were doing. You had not noticed how stiff you were.

journal.text: I took a gentle movement break after sitting still.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: persistent worry and disrupted sleep. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs $360.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

choices.label: Accept hospital assessment
Decline assessment

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: A shortcut through the execution
decisions.situation: A museum shortcut in Los Angeles takes you through a medieval punishment exhibit. A mechanical executioner swings a foam axe across the marked path. The long route has no executioner.

choices.label: Take the long route
Time the swing and walk through slowly
Sprint straight through the swinging axe

result.title: A head start
result.body: You turn back. A speaker announces, “The coward flees!” Three visitors turn to look. You continue with your head and your dignity approximately intact.

journal.text: I took the long route around a museum’s mechanical executioner.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: persistent worry and disrupted sleep. You have been diagnosed with Anxiety disorder. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs $360.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

choices.label: Accept hospital assessment
Decline assessment

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: The missing letter
decisions.situation: A poster for a free public cookery class has dropped the L from “public”. The organiser cannot work out why people keep arriving with suspicious questions.

choices.label: Point out the missing letter quietly
Leave the organiser to discover it
Read the heading aloud to the queue

result.title: A little tape saves the afternoon
result.body: The organiser repairs the heading and looks at the queue with fresh concern. The class returns to soup.

journal.text: I pointed out an embarrassing typo on a cookery-class poster.

decisions.title: Any difficult questions?
decisions.situation: At a free talk, a speaker claims nobody has ever disproved their theory. The theory is that pigeons remember your face and discuss you at night.

choices.label: Ask how they interviewed the pigeons
Let another questioner take this one
Announce that the pigeons work for you

result.title: The method needs work
result.body: They admit they inferred the conversations. You learn the difference between a suspicious bird and actual evidence.

journal.text: I questioned the evidence behind a speaker’s theory about pigeons.

decisions.title: One more attempt at your name
decisions.situation: At a local discussion group, the host mispronounces your name twice and then suggests a nickname you have never used.

choices.label: Say your name clearly once more
Turn the correction into a light joke
Use the nickname for the afternoon

result.title: A manageable correction
result.body: The host repeats it correctly and moves on. The proposed nickname retires before its first appearance.

journal.text: I corrected my name instead of accepting an unwanted nickname.

decisions.title: In loving memory of the wrong man
decisions.situation: A public meeting in Los Angeles unveils a proposed memorial bench. Its plaque honours a man who is alive, in the room, and asking whether this affects his parking permit.

choices.label: Suggest checking the plaque first
Hear the allegedly deceased man out
Leave before the eulogy

result.title: Death withdrawn from the proposal
result.body: You help redirect the discussion towards correcting the inscription. The man asks to keep “much loved” if possible.

journal.text: I suggested correcting a memorial plaque for a living man in Los Angeles.

decisions.title: The door does not believe in you
decisions.situation: An automatic shop door refuses to open for you. It opens for a child, a trolley and a blowing receipt. You step forward. Nothing. The cashier points at the sensor and suggests waving.

choices.label: Ask the cashier to let you out
Follow the trolley out
Perform an increasingly furious dance

result.title: Assisted departure
result.body: The cashier walks over. The doors open immediately for them. They hold the sensor while you leave, like a bouncer escorting out a ghost.

journal.text: I had to ask a cashier to release me through an automatic door.

decisions.title: Happy statistical decline
decisions.situation: For your birthday, someone sends a list of famous people who had achieved more by your age. They finish with “Hope this inspires you!”

choices.label: Celebrate without the comparison chart
Choose one goal that is actually yours
Read every biography before bed

result.title: Cake remains an achievement
result.body: You put the list aside. Your day improves immediately when it stops competing with a dead inventor.

journal.text: I ignored an unhelpful achievement list on my birthday.

decisions.title: A shortcut through the execution
decisions.situation: A museum shortcut in Los Angeles takes you through a medieval punishment exhibit. A mechanical executioner swings a foam axe across the marked path. The long route has no executioner.

choices.label: Take the long route
Time the swing and walk through slowly
Sprint straight through the swinging axe

result.title: A head start
result.body: You turn back. A speaker announces, “The coward flees!” Three visitors turn to look. You continue with your head and your dignity approximately intact.

journal.text: I took the long route around a museum’s mechanical executioner.

decisions.title: Before answering immediately
decisions.situation: A mildly irritating question arrives while you are already tired. You notice the sharp reply forming before the other person has finished speaking.

choices.label: Take a moment before answering
Say you need a short break
Deliver the sharp reply

result.title: A reply with less edge
result.body: The pause gives you time to separate the question from your tiredness. You answer the thing that was actually asked.

journal.text: I paused before answering sharply when I was tired.

decisions.title: Apparently you ate
decisions.situation: A younger person points at your outfit and says, “You ate.” You have no food on you. They add, “No crumbs.” This is getting less clear.

choices.label: Ask whether this is a compliment
Reply, “Thank you. It was delicious.”
Announce that you can feed yourself

result.title: Breakfast has nothing to do with it
result.body: It is a compliment. You thank them and ask for a translation before anyone says anything else about your digestion.

journal.text: I asked someone to explain a slang compliment about my outfit.

decisions.title: In loving memory of the wrong man
decisions.situation: A public meeting in Los Angeles unveils a proposed memorial bench. Its plaque honours a man who is alive, in the room, and asking whether this affects his parking permit.

choices.label: Suggest checking the plaque first
Hear the allegedly deceased man out
Leave before the eulogy

result.title: Death withdrawn from the proposal
result.body: You help redirect the discussion towards correcting the inscription. The man asks to keep “much loved” if possible.

journal.text: I suggested correcting a memorial plaque for a living man in Los Angeles.

decisions.title: Everyone here is a winner
decisions.situation: At a motivational taster session, you are asked to name your greatest achievement. The person before you says they survived eight workplace investigations. The facilitator applauds and turns to you.

choices.label: Say you got out of bed today
Ask what the investigations were about
Claim you invented motivational seminars

result.title: A standing achievement
result.body: The facilitator calls this a triumph over horizontal thinking. Everyone stands to applaud. You sit down before they can invent a course about it.

journal.text: I told a motivational group that getting out of bed was my achievement.

decisions.title: The soup tribunal
decisions.situation: You describe a bowl of soup online as “fine”. A stranger accuses you of destroying local culture. They have posted eleven replies and a diagram.

choices.label: Explain that you meant the soup
Leave the soup to its lawyers
Publish a detailed attack on their diagram

result.title: A narrow defence
result.body: You clarify that your review concerns lunch rather than civilisation. The diagram receives no further comment.

journal.text: I clarified a soup review after a stranger took it personally.

decisions.title: Money is falling from the sky
decisions.situation: A gust sends banknotes across a square in Los Angeles. You grab one before spotting a film crew and the words FOR FILM USE across the back.

choices.label: Help return the prop notes
Pose briefly like a terrible billionaire
Insist the prop note is now yours

result.title: An honest counterfeit cleanup
result.body: You collect paper money worth precisely nothing. A crew member thanks you while chasing a very wealthy-looking pigeon.

journal.text: I helped a film crew recover wind-blown prop money in Los Angeles.

decisions.title: Practice grief
decisions.situation: At a free estate-planning demonstration, volunteers act as fictional heirs. Your card says “loving relative”. The person beside you is already asking what the imaginary house is worth.

choices.label: Play the grieving relative sincerely
Ask how real inheritance rules work
Demand the imaginary house in character

result.title: A family worth inventing
result.body: You deliver a moving line about the fictional deceased. The facilitator thanks you. Your neighbour asks whether the line helped your share.

journal.text: I played a grieving relative at an estate-planning demonstration.

decisions.title: Honest feedback, preferably positive
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, you try a cracker that tastes strongly of cupboard. The demonstrator asks for a glowing testimonial while holding a camera.

choices.label: Suggest improving the flavour first
Praise how neatly it broke
Deliver a dramatic account of the cupboard

result.title: A review they can use
result.body: You mention the texture and the cupboard problem. The camera lowers. They admit this batch has been “challenging”.

journal.text: I gave specific criticism of a free food sample.

decisions.title: The important businessman
decisions.situation: You sit in the last free café chair. A child wearing an enormous tie tells you it is reserved for an important businessman. The businessman, they explain, is them.

choices.label: Ask what business they are in
Offer them the chair after your drink
Explain that reserving chairs is bad business

result.title: A volatile juice market
result.body: They explain that juice has gone up and crayons are a bad investment. You move to the counter while they hold a meeting with a biscuit.

journal.text: I gave up a café chair after hearing a child’s business plan.

decisions.title: What do you do all day?
decisions.situation: A stranger assumes you are retired and asks whether you have taken up “something gentle, like birdwatching”. You have not told them anything about your life.

choices.label: Tell them what your days actually involve
Say the birds are frightened of you
Describe every activity they failed to imagine

result.title: An overdue factual check
result.body: You give a short answer. They apologise for inventing your schedule before learning your name.

journal.text: I corrected a stranger’s assumption about my daily life.

decisions.title: Water with a personal brand
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, a presenter claims their water has been “emotionally filtered”. The jug beside it is labelled TAP. You are just thirsty.

choices.label: Drink the tap water
Ask which emotions the filter removes
Debate the emotional lives of liquids

result.title: No emotional processing required
result.body: It tastes like water. The presenter watches you finish a glass with the expression of someone witnessing sabotage.

journal.text: I chose tap water at a premium-water demonstration.

decisions.title: Older than bread
decisions.situation: A birthday cake for you arrives with an extra zero among the candles. Someone asks whether you knew the person who invented bread.

choices.label: Ask for the extra candles to be removed
Keep the cake and accept your ancient status
Deliver a speech about surviving the last ice age

result.title: A breakthrough in reverse ageing
result.body: They remove the extra candles, then stand back as though they have made you younger. You thank the bakery for its medical breakthrough.

journal.text: I corrected an extra zero on my birthday cake.

decisions.title: The quiet place has noises
decisions.situation: You sit somewhere quiet and immediately notice a clock, a distant door and somebody clearing their throat. Apparently quiet did not mean perfectly silent.

choices.label: Let the ordinary sounds be there
Choose one steady sound to notice
Identify every interruption

result.title: Quiet enough is available
result.body: You stop checking each sound for a reason to be irritated. The place becomes restful without becoming silent.

journal.text: I accepted ordinary background sounds in a quiet moment.

decisions.title: Serving suggestion: a camera
decisions.situation: An online meal looks so perfect that your ordinary food feels embarrassing. Then the creator posts a behind-the-scenes clip: the garnish is held up with glue.

choices.label: Appreciate that your food is edible
Borrow the arrangement, skip the glue
Decide your food still looks inadequate

result.title: Dinner wins on a technicality
result.body: Your meal lacks dramatic lighting. It also lacks craft adhesive, which feels like a reasonable compromise.

decisions.title: Help has been offered
decisions.situation: Someone offers a hand with a small practical task. You are not sure you need the help, but you notice yourself preparing a defence before considering the offer.

choices.label: Accept if the help would be useful
Politely decline and explain your preference
Treat the offer as an insult

result.title: A task shared

journal.text: I accepted useful help with a small task.

decisions.title: Beginners’ self-defence
decisions.situation: At a free beginner lesson, the instructor asks you to demonstrate a firm “No!” You give one so convincing that a passer-by apologises and leaves.

choices.label: Practise the rest of the lesson
Watch the demonstrations first
Use your new “No!” on the whole lesson

result.title: A useful loud afternoon
result.body: You learn the basics and repeat the shout. The corridor remains unusually clear for the rest of the lesson.

journal.text: I practised the basics at a free self-defence lesson.

decisions.title: A very local tragedy
decisions.situation: On a free history walk in Los Angeles, the guide points at a laundrette: “A forbidden romance began here.” The owner leans out and asks whether this is about the washing-machine warranty.

choices.label: Stay for both versions
Ask the owner for the real story
Leave before the historical reenactment

result.title: Star-crossed and spin-dried
result.body: The guide describes a doomed affair. The owner describes a parts supplier. You finish the walk unsure which relationship suffered more.

journal.text: I heard two competing tragedies outside a laundrette in Los Angeles.

decisions.title: Your shoulders have a complaint
decisions.situation: After sitting in the same position for a while, you notice that your shoulders appear to have crept up towards your ears.

choices.label: Take a gentle movement break
Change your position and relax your shoulders
Stay exactly as you are

result.title: A different position helps
result.body: You loosen up at a comfortable pace and return to what you were doing. You had not noticed how stiff you were.

journal.text: I took a gentle movement break after sitting still.

decisions.title: A number with nowhere to go
decisions.situation: You suddenly remember a telephone number you have not used for years. You cannot remember what you entered a room to fetch, but the number is perfect.

choices.label: Enjoy the memory’s strange priorities
Return calmly to the original task
Treat the distraction as a personal crisis

result.title: An impressive useless recital
result.body: You repeat the number once and laugh at the timing. Memory has supplied an answer to a question nobody asked.

journal.text: I remembered an old telephone number at an unhelpful moment.

decisions.title: The sofa is judging you
decisions.situation: Autoplay follows your programme with a competitive fitness class. A man who appears to have been assembled entirely from elbows challenges you to beat your personal best.

choices.label: Switch to the beginner version and try it
Invent a chair-based version
Keep up with him at full speed

result.title: An achievable number of elbows
result.body: You complete the gentler routine. The instructor says anyone can do it, then folds himself into a shape you decline to investigate.

journal.text: I followed a beginner workout after a fitness video appeared on autoplay.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: persistent unexplained fatigue and changes in health. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs $2,160.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

choices.label: Accept hospital assessment
Decline assessment

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: It cannot have been this bad
decisions.situation: You revisit a comedy you have called your favourite for years. Ten minutes in, a man falls into a bucket for the fourth time. You appear to have remembered a much better programme.

choices.label: Admit your taste has improved
Work out what you used to enjoy
Watch the whole thing out of loyalty

result.title: The bucket loses a fan
result.body: You stop watching without trying to defend your younger self in court. There are other ways to spend the evening.

journal.text: I stopped pretending to enjoy an old favourite programme.

decisions.title: You said that part out loud
decisions.situation: You rehearse a devastating comeback while walking. A stranger turns around just as you announce, “That is why nobody trusts your ferret.”

choices.label: Explain that you were arguing in your head
Write the useful point down privately
Pretend to be on an important phone call

result.title: No actual ferret dispute
result.body: The stranger accepts the explanation and walks on a little faster. You retire the argument before it recruits anyone else.

journal.text: I stopped an imaginary argument after saying part of it aloud.

decisions.title: An ordinary morning
decisions.situation: The morning is quiet. You finish your tea before anyone asks you for anything. This feels suspiciously well organised.

choices.label: Enjoy it as it is
Get in touch with someone
Look for something to worry about

result.title: A second cup, still no emergency
result.body: You make more tea and do absolutely nothing impressive. It is an excellent use of the morning.

journal.text: I enjoyed a quiet morning and a second cup of tea.

decisions.title: Before answering immediately
decisions.situation: A mildly irritating question arrives while you are already tired. You notice the sharp reply forming before the other person has finished speaking.

choices.label: Take a moment before answering
Say you need a short break
Deliver the sharp reply

result.title: A reply with less edge
result.body: The pause gives you time to separate the question from your tiredness. You answer the thing that was actually asked.

journal.text: I paused before answering sharply when I was tired.

decisions.title: Serving suggestion: a camera
decisions.situation: An online meal looks so perfect that your ordinary food feels embarrassing. Then the creator posts a behind-the-scenes clip: the garnish is held up with glue.

choices.label: Appreciate that your food is edible
Borrow the arrangement, skip the glue
Decide your food still looks inadequate

result.title: Dinner wins on a technicality
result.body: Your meal lacks dramatic lighting. It also lacks craft adhesive, which feels like a reasonable compromise.
